messages:
selene: Quick follow-up from the RFC: I'm trying to nail down the cutover plan for the 'slab tracing' + API choreography refactor. We need a low-risk path to migrate clients off the old enrichment endpoint and pay down the old surface. Thoughts on sequential vs parallel cutover?
vikram: Sequential seems safer for traffic-heavy tenants. Parallel helps us iterate faster but increases coordination cost. Prefer canary-by-tenant first.
maya: +1 for tenant canaries. Also want to ensure we have a visible KPI early: 95th latency and error ratio per route during canary windows.
kenji: Agreed. We should lock the compatibility shim for 2 weeks after the final cut to allow slow clients to migrate. Add a feature flag to toggle shim read/write.
selene: Proposal: 3-phase plan -> (1) rollout new light API (api/v2/enrich-lite) behind flag, (2) route 5% of traffic by tenant for 48h, monitor, (3) escalate to 25/50/100 with rollback gates. Keep old endpoint read-only after 50% for 7 days.
vikram: What about batching semantics? v2 changes the KV prefix behavior slightly. We need an adapter layer in the runtime to map old prefixes during the migration window. That's non-trivial but doable.
maya: Can we quantify risk? If adapter adds 1-2ms p99, that's acceptable. If it spikes error budgets, we rollback. Define acceptable thresholds now.
kenji: Suggested thresholds: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms, error rate increase < 0.25% absolute. If any threshold violates for >15m, auto-failover to old path.
selene: We'll park those in the rollout doc. Who owns the auto-failover play? @infra-sre?
infra-sre: I can own the failover hooks and the runbook. I want a simple CLI to flip routes and a metric to track last successful switch.
kenji: I'll add a small endpoint to the router: POST /_admin/route-switch {"service":"enricher","target":"legacy"} with RBAC. Keep it guarded.
selene: Pseudo-command for ops for emergency:

```
# switch all tenants back to legacy in emergency
curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \n  https://router.internal/_admin/route-switch -d '{"service":"enricher","target":"legacy","scope":"all"}'
```

selene: We'll store that in the incident runbook.
maya: We also need observability changes: span names should carry migration-variant tag (old|v2|shim) so we can slice traces easily. Add it to the tracing schema RFC.
vikram: +1 — also emit a migration_event counter per request so we can build a heatmap of leftover traffic.
kenji: For tech-debt paydown: we should schedule a follow-up sprint to remove the shim and old endpoint once adoption <1% for 14 days. Who signs off that deletion?
selene: Product needs to own the deletion sign-off but engineering must provide adoption metrics. Let's add a kill date proposal in the RFC and require a rollback window.
infra-sre: Note: removing endpoint will affect monitoring dashboards. We'll prepare a deprecation checklist: alert updates, grafana dashboards, docs, client library notices.
maya: Let's also create a small eval harness to run the old vs new path on the same inputs to sanity-check outputs before wide rollout. Small sample set, not full A/B.
vikram: Good idea. Who owns the harness? I can spin up a quick harness in eng-ml to compare outputs for 48h.
kenji: On the code side: prefer to gate the shim behind a config flag in the router, not in the service binary, so we can flip without deploys.
selene: Action items I see: 1) infra-sre: failover hooks + runbook (ETA Tue), 2) kenji: route-switch endpoint + feature flag (ETA Wed), 3) vikram: harness + KV-prefix adapter spike (ETA Thu), 4) maya: tracing schema + KPI dashboard (ETA Thu). I'll update RFC doc with these and ping product for deletion sign-off cadence.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary pipeline triggered for enricher-refactor:v2 -> canary-1 (5% tenants). Started at 2026-03-12T10:45:12Z.
maya: I'll watch dashboards during the canary window. Ping me if anything crosses thresholds.
selene: Thanks team — we'll reconvene after the 48h canary. If anyone spots a hidden dependency (client libs, partner integrations), add it to the RFC checklist now. :thumbsup:
